report:
## Does Ginkgo Biloba Relieve Tinnitus? — Evidence Summary

**Conclusion: The evidence does not support ginkgo biloba as an effective treatment for tinnitus.**

The most authoritative source is the Cochrane systematic review, the gold standard for evaluating medical evidence. According to a summary of this review, "the Cochrane systematic review on ginkgo biloba for tinnitus concluded that there was no reliable evidence that ginkgo reduces tinnitus severity compared to placebo" (https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/).

This aligns with a key randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial combined with a meta-analysis of prior randomized trials by Rejali, Sivakumar, and Balaji, published in *Clinical Otolaryngology*, titled "Ginkgo biloba does not benefit patients with tinnitus" (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1365-2273.2004.00814.x). This study explicitly concluded no benefit, and its findings are echoed across multiple review articles in the search results.

There is some conflicting industry-funded research: a manufacturer (Schwabe) sponsored study on their specific extract (EGb 761®) reported positive results in an open-label, uncontrolled trial of 170 patients (https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0383/15/1/87). However, this study design—lacking a placebo control—is far weaker evidence than randomized controlled trials, since it cannot rule out placebo effects or natural symptom fluctuation, which are common in tinnitus.

Some earlier systematic reviews of specific EGb 761 formulations found modest positive effects in a subset of trials, illustrating inconsistency in the literature depending on formulation, dosage, and study quality.

**Bottom line:** The strongest, most rigorous evidence (Cochrane review, placebo-controlled RCT with meta-analysis) indicates ginkgo biloba does not reliably relieve tinnitus symptoms. Positive findings tend to come from lower-quality, uncontrolled, or industry-sponsored studies.
